chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ubaydi, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the woman who leads the women in prayer: what is the limit of raising her voice during the recitation or the takbir? He said, 'To the extent that they can hear her.'

key_terms.بِقَدْرِ مَا تُسْمِعُ: to the extent that she makes them hear

ai.seo_question: What is the limit of a woman's voice when leading other women in prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the criterion for a woman's vocal volume during prayer is defined functionally as 'just enough to be heard' (bi-qadri ma tasma'u), distinguishing it from the louder recitation of men. This ruling, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the Shia juristic consensus that women's recitation in congregational prayer should be audible to the immediate female followers but not necessarily to men or the general public, emphasizing modesty and clarity in worship.
